poverty_rate.label: People in poverty
poverty_rate.note: People whose family income is below the federal poverty line (C17002). ± is the 90% margin of error.
poverty_rate.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

near_poverty_share.label: People just above the poverty line (100% to 199%)
near_poverty_share.note: People whose family income is between 100% and 199% of the federal poverty line (C17002). ± is the 90% margin of error.
near_poverty_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

below_200_share.label: People below 200% of the poverty line
below_200_share.note: People in poverty plus those just above it (C17002). For a family of four in 2024, 200% of the poverty line was about $62,400 a year. ± is the 90% margin of error.
below_200_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

median_household_income.label: Median household income
median_household_income.note: Half of households earn more and half earn less, in 2024 dollars (B19013). The district figure is estimated from its income brackets (B19001), because medians cannot be added up across tracts.
median_household_income.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

snap_households_share.label: Households that got SNAP food aid
snap_households_share.note: Households that received SNAP at any time in the past 12 months, as reported in the survey (B22003). Surveys tend to undercount program use. ± is the 90% margin of error.
snap_households_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

rent_burden.label: Renters paying 30% or more of income on rent
rent_burden.note: Renter households whose gross rent is 30% or more of household income (B25070). ± is the 90% margin of error.
rent_burden.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

owner_cost_burden.label: Owners with a mortgage paying 30% or more on housing
owner_cost_burden.note: Owner households with a mortgage whose monthly costs are 30% or more of household income (B25091). ± is the 90% margin of error.
owner_cost_burden.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

prime_age_epop.label: Prime-age workers: share of people 25 to 54 with a job
prime_age_epop.note: People 25 to 54 who are employed (civilian jobs plus armed forces) as a share of all people 25 to 54 (B23001). Tracts with a prison, college dorms or a nursing home can show a low rate because those residents rarely hold jobs. ± is the 90% margin of error.
prime_age_epop.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

bachelors_or_higher.label: Adults with a bachelor's degree or more
bachelors_or_higher.note: Adults 25 and older whose highest degree is a bachelor's or higher (B15003). ± is the 90% margin of error.
bachelors_or_higher.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

hs_or_higher.label: Adults with a high school diploma or more
hs_or_higher.note: Adults 25 and older with a high school diploma, GED or higher (B15003). ± is the 90% margin of error.
hs_or_higher.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

uninsured_acs.label: People without health insurance
uninsured_acs.note: Civilians not in institutions with no health insurance at the time of the survey (B27010). ± is the 90% margin of error.
uninsured_acs.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

medicaid_share.label: People with Medicaid or other means-tested coverage
medicaid_share.note: Civilians not in institutions with Medicaid or other means-tested public coverage (C27007). The survey tends to undercount Medicaid. ± is the 90% margin of error.
medicaid_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

disability_share.label: People with a disability
disability_share.note: Civilians not in institutions reporting a hearing, vision, thinking, walking, self-care or independent-living difficulty (B18101). ± is the 90% margin of error.
disability_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

population.label: Population (ACS)
population.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

prime_age_share.label: Residents ages 25 to 54
prime_age_share.note: Share of all residents who are 25 to 54 (B01001). ± is the 90% margin of error.
prime_age_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

age65_share.label: Residents 65 and older
age65_share.note: Share of all residents who are 65 or older (B01001). ± is the 90% margin of error.
age65_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

nh_white_share.label: White, not Hispanic
nh_white_share.note: Share of all residents (B03002). Race groups are people who reported one race and are not Hispanic. ± is the 90% margin of error.
nh_white_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

nh_black_share.label: Black, not Hispanic
nh_black_share.note: Share of all residents (B03002). ± is the 90% margin of error.
nh_black_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

hispanic_share.label: Hispanic or Latino (any race)
hispanic_share.note: Share of all residents (B03002). Hispanic or Latino people can be of any race. ± is the 90% margin of error.
hispanic_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

nh_asian_share.label: Asian, not Hispanic
nh_asian_share.note: Share of all residents (B03002). ± is the 90% margin of error.
nh_asian_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

nh_multi_share.label: Two or more races, not Hispanic
nh_multi_share.note: Share of all residents (B03002). ± is the 90% margin of error.
nh_multi_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

nh_other_share.label: Another race, not Hispanic
nh_other_share.note: American Indian or Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander, or some other race, not Hispanic (B03002). With the five groups above, the groups add to 100%. ± is the 90% margin of error.
nh_other_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

foreign_born_share.label: Foreign-born residents
foreign_born_share.note: Residents who were not U.S. citizens at birth, including naturalized citizens (B05012). People born abroad to U.S.-citizen parents, or in Puerto Rico or another U.S. territory, are native-born. ± is the 90% margin of error.
foreign_born_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

female_share.label: Residents who are female
female_share.note: Share of all residents who are female (B01001). The survey counts sex, not gender identity. ± is the 90% margin of error.
female_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

places_diabetes.label: Adults with diagnosed diabetes
places_diabetes.source: CDC, PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, Census Tract Data, 2025 release
places_diabetes.note: Modeled estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. Not a direct count; tracts close to each other can look alike because the model shares information across areas. ± is half the width of the 95% interval.

places_obesity.label: Adults with obesity
places_obesity.source: CDC, PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, Census Tract Data, 2025 release
places_obesity.note: Modeled estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. Not a direct count; tracts close to each other can look alike because the model shares information across areas. ± is half the width of the 95% interval.

places_depression.label: Adults ever told they have depression
places_depression.source: CDC, PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, Census Tract Data, 2025 release
places_depression.note: Modeled estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. Not a direct count; tracts close to each other can look alike because the model shares information across areas. ± is half the width of the 95% interval.

places_mental_distress.label: Adults with frequent mental distress
places_mental_distress.source: CDC, PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, Census Tract Data, 2025 release
places_mental_distress.note: Modeled estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. Not a direct count; tracts close to each other can look alike because the model shares information across areas. ± is half the width of the 95% interval.

places_smoking.label: Adults who currently smoke cigarettes
places_smoking.source: CDC, PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, Census Tract Data, 2025 release
places_smoking.note: Modeled estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. Not a direct count; tracts close to each other can look alike because the model shares information across areas. ± is half the width of the 95% interval.

places_checkup.label: Adults with a routine checkup in the past year
places_checkup.source: CDC, PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, Census Tract Data, 2025 release
places_checkup.note: Modeled estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. Not a direct count; tracts close to each other can look alike because the model shares information across areas. ± is half the width of the 95% interval.

places_food_insecurity.label: Adults with food insecurity in the past year
places_food_insecurity.source: CDC, PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, Census Tract Data, 2025 release
places_food_insecurity.note: Modeled estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. Not a direct count; tracts close to each other can look alike because the model shares information across areas. ± is half the width of the 95% interval.

places_no_transportation.label: Adults without reliable transportation in the past year
places_no_transportation.source: CDC, PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, Census Tract Data, 2025 release
places_no_transportation.note: Modeled estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. Not a direct count; tracts close to each other can look alike because the model shares information across areas. ± is half the width of the 95% interval.

unemployment_rate.label: Unemployment rate
unemployment_rate.note: Share of the labor force without a job and looking for one. People are counted where they live, not where they work. County figures come from a BLS model, not a direct count.

avg_weekly_wage.label: Average weekly wage
avg_weekly_wage.source: BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
avg_weekly_wage.note: Average weekly pay per job, all employers including government. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation. Jobs are counted where the job is, not where the worker lives. Covers jobs under state unemployment insurance and, in the all-ownership total, federal civilian jobs.

uninsured_under65.label: Uninsured rate, under age 65
uninsured_under65.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Small Area Health Insurance Estimates (SAHIE)
uninsured_under65.note: Share of people under 65 with no health insurance. SAHIE is a model-based estimate that combines survey and administrative records; the margin shown is the 90% margin of error.

saipe_child_poverty_rate.label: Child poverty rate, ages 0 to 17 (annual)
saipe_child_poverty_rate.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (SAIPE)
saipe_child_poverty_rate.note: Share of children under 18 below the federal poverty line. SAIPE is a model-based estimate that combines survey, tax and SNAP records, so it gives one value per year; the margin shown is the 90% margin of error.

overdose_rate_per100k.label: Drug overdose deaths per 100,000 people, past 12 months
overdose_rate_per100k.source: CDC NCHS, VSRR Provisional County-Level Drug Overdose Death Counts; Census Bureau population estimates
overdose_rate_per100k.note: Our calculation: provisional 12-month deaths divided by the Census July 1 population for the year the period ends (2025 population for 2026 periods), times 100,000. Not age-adjusted; blank where CDC hides counts of 1 to 9.

pop_change_pct.label: Population change since 2020
pop_change_pct.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program
pop_change_pct.note: Percent change from the April 1, 2020 estimates base to July 1 of each year. The base is the 2020 Census count adjusted by the Census Bureau, not the raw count.
